claim: A submission can score EXACTLY 0.0 with no error raised if any predicted edge links non-consecutive timepoints; GT edges only ever connect t->t+1, so stride/frame-skipping for speed makes every edge structurally unmatchable.
quote: Ground truth edges only ever connect strictly consecutive timepoints (t -> t+1). An edge between non-consecutive frames can never match a GT edge under the official metric, so every single edge I submitted was structurally unmatchable — TP=0 across the board

claim: The fix for the exact-0.0 trap is to process a CONTIGUOUS block of frames from t=0 per dataset (sized to the time budget) rather than subsampling with a stride; the same pipeline went 0.0 -> 0.366 -> 0.380.
quote: instead of subsampling with a stride, process a contiguous block of frames from t=0 for each dataset (sized proportionally to the global time budget). This guarantees every edge connects t and t+1. Went from 0.0 -> 0.366 -> 0.380

claim: A zero-score submission gives no diagnostic signal: the CSV validates, all datasets present, all columns correct, and it silently returns 0.0 — so a local round-trip format check does NOT protect against it.
quote: No format error was raised (the file was valid CSV, all columns correct, all datasets present), so it silently scored 0.0 with no diagnostic signal.

claim: The scoring rerun processes ~200 hidden volumes and routinely takes 5-12 hours wall clock, against a 12-hour hard limit; multiple teams have lost runs to Notebook Timeout after a notebook that ran in minutes on the 4 visible test clips.
quote:
Notebook successful completed its end to end execution against test data in 637s using GPU T4 x2.

*But the actual submission(i.e scoring) took 7hrs.*

claim: Rerun-vs-visible-test time ratio is roughly 50x: the 4 visible test clips are a smoke test, not a runtime estimate.
quote: it takes ~50x longer than running notebook i think

claim: Scoring times of 8-11 hours are reported as normal by multiple participants, leaving very little headroom under the 12h limit.
quote:
Mine takes between 8-9hrs
--- Mine is on 11th hour

claim: At least one team hit Notebook Timeout on the scored rerun after completing in ~5.6h against the visible test clips; nobody (including the host) answered whether the rerun limit is the same 12h as Code Requirements states.
quote: Our submission notebook completes successfully in ~5.6h against the visible test clips, but the actual scored rerun came back as Notebook Timeout with no public score.

claim: The visible test set is deliberately minimal so notebooks verify in 15-30 minutes; the hidden test set swapped in is approximately the size of the ~88 GB, 199-volume training set.
quote: the visible verification dataset is intentionally kept minimal to allow rapid notebook saving and verification in 15-30 minutes. However ... the hidden test set swapped in during final evaluation ... is roughly the exact same size as the ~88 GB training dataset.

claim: Pip-installing packages at runtime breaks submission: the notebook is flagged as using the internet even after internet is disabled; dependencies must be pre-staged as attached datasets.
quote:
I keep getting a message saying my notebook is using the internet. I've disabled it and saved the changes, yet the notification telling me to disconnect the notebook from the internet keeps popping up
--- These won't work during submission

claim: A pre-built CSV copied to submission.csv cannot work: the test folder is replaced by private samples at rerun, so dataset names must be discovered at runtime by globbing the input tree.
quote: pre built csv won't work, the test folder is replaced by private samples during submission. The submission file is expected to have nodes, edges from all the given datasets in the private test folder.

claim: A 7-submission diagnostic found 'Submission Scoring Error' is triggered by node timepoints exceeding a dataset's real frame count, not by row count, topology, branching or coordinate values; the boundary was between t=5 (works) and t=9 (fails).
quote: an earlier test with the same coordinate and topology extended to t=0 through t=9 (10 nodes, 9 edges) failed with Scoring Error. So the real trigger looks tied to the timepoint range ... submissions with t values beyond a dataset's actual frame count get rejected outright

claim: Dynamic runtime discovery of test dataset names with zero edges scores successfully, giving a cheap structural smoke-test submission that isolates format problems from scoring problems.
quote: I built a submission that discovers the test dataset names dynamically at runtime (globbing /kaggle/input/*/test/.zarr, no hardcoded names) and writes one node per dataset at t=0 with no edges at all ... yet it succeeded (score 0.000)

claim: Public LB is reported as roughly 10% more optimistic than a held-out CV, with very large movie-to-movie variance: +/-0.14, 18% coefficient of variation, worst movie 0.460 and best 0.984.
quote: the public LB is more optimistic by almost 10%. That being said, movie-to-movie variability is large: ±0.14, with 18% coefficient of variation. Worst movie scores 0.460 and the best is at 0.984. The public split might have more of the easy movies compared to my hold out set.

claim: The public checkpoints were trained on all 199 annotated videos, so any CV using those weights on train videos is scoring a memorised model.
quote: The public weights were trained on all 199 annotated videos. Their split_manifest.json lists 199 under train, and the 40 in its own test list are all inside that same set. So if you're validating on train videos with those checkpoints, you're scoring the model on data it memorized.

claim: A training-set harness inverts the sign of post-processing ablations: a measured +0.0184 from disabling one corrective stage became 0.909 vs a 0.912 baseline on LB.
quote: I ablated the post-processing in the public pipeline and measured +0.0184 from turning one stage off ... Submitted it and got 0.909 against my 0.912 baseline. The sign flipped ... A training-set harness will keep telling you to delete the components that matter most at test time.

claim: Multiple teams independently report that linker/motion-model improvements worth +0.012 to +0.04 on 5-fold CV convert to exactly +0.001 on the public LB.
quote: My motion linker changes give around +0.012 on 5-fold CV on average, with no fold getting worse, but the LB gain is exactly +0.001.

claim: The 0.946-class public notebook scores ~0.015 WORSE than a private 0.942 notebook under the same 5-fold local CV - direct evidence of public-test overfitting in the shared public lineage.
quote: I also compared the public 0.946 LB notebook with my older private 0.942 LB notebook under the same 5-fold CV setup, and surprisingly the public one was about 0.015 worse locally.

claim: CV-LB direction is not consistent across teams: some report CV pessimistic by 0.013-0.02 vs public LB while others report CV 0.96 against LB 0.93, so no team's published CV offset transfers.
quote: nearly all my local CV scores are more pessimistic than the public LB by about ~0.013-0.02 ... I have like 0.96 CV and 0.93 LB for some reason

claim: The one concrete anti-shakeup discipline proposed in the shakeup thread is to decompose CV into edge_jaccard, adjusted_edge_jaccard, node recall, node count, division jaccard, track breaks and mislinks rather than report a single number.
quote:
it is not useful to state/anayse " 0.96 CV "
you should break it down:
edge_jaccard = ???
adjusted_edge_jaccard = ???
node recall = ...
estimated no of nodes = ...
division = ...
breaks in tracks ....
link to wrong trajectory ....

claim: Leave-one-embryo-out is the community-consensus CV, but it requires training your own detector because every released checkpoint has seen both embryos.
quote: Leave-one-embryo-out is the right call, though as Adarsh says it means training your own model, since the released checkpoints have seen everything.

claim: An exact public-LB split of the two score terms costs ONE submission: summarise() drops the division term when a submission contains no divisions, so a fork-free submission returns pure adjusted edge Jaccard.
quote: summarise() drops the division term entirely when a submission contains no divisions at all (score = edge_jaccard if not has_divisions). So a fork-free submission returns your pure adjusted edge Jaccard, and the division term follows by subtraction
